title: I2C overview: shared bus, segmentation and cable review
summary: Select a shared bus or explicitly translated/segmented connection. Establish mode, addresses and electrical loading before choosing pull-ups.
applies_to: Standard-mode, Fast-mode and Fast-mode Plus I2C; selected devices must support the chosen mode.
required_inputs: Devices, addresses, bus mode and pull-up supply
Clock stretching, capacitance and power sequence
verification: Review compatibility and read the linked pull-up and topology guides.
limitations: I3C, SMBus, PMBus, Hs-mode and Ultra-Fast mode are outside these patterns.

citations.locator: Sections 2, 5 and 6: physical layer, reserved addresses and advanced topics

title: I2C shared open-drain bus pattern
summary: Connect SDA and SCL as shared open-drain nets with a compatible pull-up supply. Include every fitted pull-up in the resistance calculation.
applies_to: Standard-mode, Fast-mode and Fast-mode Plus I2C; selected devices must support the chosen mode.
required_inputs: Mode, addresses, capacitance and weakest sink specification
verification: Check address conflicts, effective resistance, rise time and LOW voltage.
limitations: Do not copy a default pull-up value or treat SDA/SCL as a differential pair.

citations.locator: Sections 2, 5 and 6: physical layer, reserved addresses and advanced topics

pattern.diagram:
VPU -- R_SDA -- SDA: Controller, Target1, Target2
VPU -- R_SCL -- SCL: Controller, Target1, Target2
Common signal ground
placement: Group bus devices to control parasitic loading.
routing: Keep branches short and separate from switching aggressors.
return_path: Use a continuous reference; see the linked shared return guidance.
pitfalls: Address conflicts cannot be corrected by PCB routing.

title: I2C translated or buffered segment pattern
summary: Use a compatible bidirectional translator or buffer when the voltage or loading analysis requires it; review each segment separately.
applies_to: Standard-mode, Fast-mode and Fast-mode Plus I2C; selected devices must support the chosen mode.
required_inputs: Translator/buffer part, mode and power sequence
Per-segment pull-ups, capacitance, delay and LOW-level offsets
verification: Check combined timing and LOW/HIGH margins, including powered-off behavior.
limitations: A pass-FET translator need not isolate capacitance. Buffer cascading and clock stretching require device review.

pattern.diagram:
V_A -> pull-ups -> SDA_A/SCL_A <-> selected device <-> SDA_B/SCL_B <- pull-ups <- V_B
Both lines require the selected bidirectional behavior
placement: Place the chosen device at the planned electrical segment boundary.
routing: Budget each side's load and the selected device's transfer behavior.
return_path: Maintain the required reference; translation alone is not galvanic isolation.
pitfalls: An ordinary push-pull translator may not support arbitration or stretching.

title: I2C cable and off-board routing pattern
summary: Include cable capacitance, crosstalk and returns in the bus review. Evaluate a buffered or differential extension if the direct bus cannot meet requirements.
applies_to: Standard-mode, Fast-mode and Fast-mode Plus I2C; selected devices must support the chosen mode.
required_inputs: Cable geometry, capacitance, noise exposure and mode
verification: Measure rise time, LOW voltage and noise at both ends with the intended cable.
limitations: No fixed cable distance guarantees operation; a differential extender needs its own datasheet and termination plan.

citations.locator: Sections 7.1-7.2 and 7.5: pull-ups, segmentation and bus wiring

pattern.diagram:
SDA ---------------- SDA   (with its return)
SCL ---------------- SCL   (with its return)
Shared reference / chosen extension hardware
placement: Place selected protection at the cable boundary.
routing: Avoid treating SDA and SCL as a twisted pair together; review coupling and loading.
return_path: For twisted-pair wiring, pair each signal with a ground return as described in UM10204 section 7.5.
pitfalls: Protection and cable capacitance consume the same bus loading budget.
